<timestamp>Friday, Nov 20, 2026, 8:59 AM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
A Cursor Desktop user on macOS (Cursor 'Glass' agents UI; the app reports darwin 27.2) wants to create a Cursor Project named 'Semiconductor' backed by the GitHub repo wolf359-ai/semiconductor and move/continue an existing agent chat into it. They could NOT find a command called 'Open Agents Window' in the command palette. From the Cursor docs, find: (1) whether 'Projects' exist in Cursor Desktop and the exact, current UI path to create one (menu names, sidebar location, command palette command names, keyboard shortcuts); (2) whether an existing chat/agent can be moved into a project, and how; (3) if Projects are a web/cloud-agents feature (cursor.com/agents) instead, the exact steps there. Quote the relevant doc text and give doc URLs. If the docs don't cover something, say so explicitly rather than guessing.
</user_query>
I'll start by fetching the Cursor docs index to find pages on Projects and the agents window.
There are dedicated Projects pages in both the docs and the help center. Fetching them alongside the Agents Window page.

The Projects page has the core answers. I'll check the Cloud Agents docs for anything about creating Projects on the web (cursor.com/agents), plus the Projects API.

I'm wondering whether the cursor.com/agents web docs might cover projects too, so I'll check the cloud-agent docs and the API create-project endpoint. I'll also grep the cloud-agent page for any mention of "Glass."

Projects do exist in Cursor Desktop, but they live in the Agents Window's sidebar and run on Cloud Agents. The docs give no command-palette command or keyboard shortcut for creating one. The missing "Open Agents Window" command most likely means the user is already in the Agents Window.

**1. Creating a Project in Desktop**

From [docs/agent/projects](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects):

> "Projects live in the left-hand nav of the Agents Window and run on Cloud Agents."

> "In the Agents Window, find the **Projects** section in the sidebar and click **New Project**."
> "Choose an icon and enter a project name. If you leave the name empty, the Project is called New Project."
> "Under **Workspace**, pick the repository the Project works in. Projects run in the cloud, so the list shows the repositories available to your cloud agents. If GitHub isn't connected yet, the menu offers **Connect GitHub**. Under **Model**, pick the model the coordinator uses."
> "Click **Create Project**. The Project opens as a chat with its coordinator."

So the steps for this user are:
1. In the Agents Window, go to the left sidebar.
2. Under **Projects**, click **New Project**.
3. Name it `Semiconductor`.
4. Under **Workspace**, pick `wolf359-ai/semiconductor`. If it's not listed, use **Connect GitHub** first.
5. Pick a model and click **Create Project**.

About the missing command, from [docs/agent/agents-window](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window):

> "If you're in the editor, type Cmd+Shift+P → Open Agents Window to open the Agents Window."
> "To return to the classic Cursor IDE, type Cmd+Shift+P → Open IDE."

That command is only described as running from the editor. The docs never mention a "Glass" UI. My guess is that the user's agents UI is the Agents Window, which would explain why the command doesn't appear; the docs don't confirm this. If they see **Open IDE** in the command palette, they're in the Agents Window.

Requirements from the Projects page:
- **Plan:** "available on every plan that includes Cloud Agents: Premium and higher, Teams, Enterprise, and legacy paid Cursor plans… isn't available on Free, Plus, or the legacy Hobby plan."
- **Privacy:** "It also isn't available with Privacy Mode (Legacy)."
- **Enterprise version:** "Enterprise teams need Cursor 3.21.9 or later."

If the **Projects** section is missing from the sidebar, the plan or the Privacy Mode setting is the likely cause.

**2. Moving an existing chat into a Project**

This is supported, with limits. From the "Add and remove chats" section of the same page:

> "Drag an eligible top-level Cloud Agent chat from the sidebar onto a Project row to add it. You can also open the chat's sidebar menu and choose **Add to Project**. If the action is available for a local chat, Cursor converts it to Remote Control before adding it. The chat then appears under the Project row and in the Agents list above the Project's chat input."

> "To take a chat out, open its menu in the Agents list and choose **Remove from Project**."

So the user can drag the chat onto the `Semiconductor` row, or use the chat's sidebar menu and pick **Add to Project**. Only top-level Cloud Agent chats are guaranteed to work. A local chat works only "if the action is available," and the docs don't say when it is. If **Add to Project** doesn't appear for their local chat, the docs offer no other way to move it.

**3. Projects on the web (cursor.com/agents)**

The docs give no steps for creating a Project in the web UI. The only Projects UI they describe is the Agents Window sidebar. What they do say about the web:
- The API's Project `url` field is described as the "URL to view the Project in Cursor Web," with the form `https://cursor.com/agents/bc-…`.
- Creating Projects in code is documented ([Create A Project](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#create-a-project)): "To create and manage Projects from code, use the Projects endpoints of the Cloud Agents API." For this case that's `POST /v1/projects` with `"name": "Semiconductor"` and `repos: [{ "url": "https://github.com/wolf359-ai/semiconductor" }]`. It needs a user API key, because a service account key returns `403 user_required`.

The API has no endpoint for adding an existing chat to a Project. Update A Project only changes the name and appearance.

**Not covered by the docs:** a keyboard shortcut or command-palette command for New Project; the "Glass" name; when **Add to Project** is available for local chats; and web UI steps for creating a Project or moving a chat into one.

Sources: [Projects](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects), [Agents Window](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window), [Cloud Agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent), [Cloud Agents API, Projects section](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#create-a-project), [Help: What is a Cursor Project?](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/projects)

I've confirmed the docs don't spell out how to create Projects in the cursor.com/agents web UI, though the API response points to a "Cursor Web" view of the Project. They place Projects in the left-hand nav of the Agents Window and never mention "Glass." My guess is that someone already in the Glass agents interface is effectively in the Agents Window, so I'll flag that as an inference rather than a fact.

No keyboard shortcut exists for creating a new Project, and the requirements are a Cloud Agents plan, Privacy Mode turned off (Legacy), and GitHub connected. Moving a chat only works for cloud agent chats, and local chats can be converted to Remote Control if that action shows up, which is likely relevant since this user's chat probably lives in the Desktop workspace.

They run on Cloud Agents, need a Premium-or-higher, Teams, Enterprise or legacy paid plan, and don't work with Privacy Mode (Legacy). To move a chat in, drag it onto the Project row or choose Add to Project from its sidebar menu; only Cloud Agent chats are guaranteed to work. The docs list no command-palette command or shortcut for New Project, and no web steps for creating one (only the API).

content.text:
Yes, Projects exist in Cursor Desktop. In the Agents Window's left sidebar, find the **Projects** section and click **New Project**. The docs give no command-palette command or keyboard shortcut for creating one.

**1. Creating the Project**

From [Projects](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects): "Projects live in the left-hand nav of the Agents Window and run on Cloud Agents." The steps are:
1. Click **New Project** in the sidebar's **Projects** section.
2. Choose an icon and enter the name `Semiconductor`.
3. Under **Workspace**, pick `wolf359-ai/semiconductor`. The docs say: "If GitHub isn't connected yet, the menu offers **Connect GitHub**."
4. Under **Model**, pick the coordinator's model.
5. Click **Create Project**. "The Project opens as a chat with its coordinator."

**Why "Open Agents Window" was missing:** [Agents Window](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window) says, "If you're in the editor, type Cmd+Shift+P → Open Agents Window." That command is only for the editor, and the reverse command is **Open IDE**. The docs never mention "Glass", but my guess is the user is already in the Agents Window. If **Open IDE** shows up in their command palette, that confirms it.

**If there's no Projects section:** Projects need a plan that includes Cloud Agents (Premium or higher, Teams, Enterprise, or a legacy paid plan). They're "not available on Free, Plus, or the legacy Hobby plan," and not with "Privacy Mode (Legacy)." Enterprise teams need Cursor 3.21.9 or later.

**2. Moving the existing chat in**

From the same page: "Drag an eligible top-level Cloud Agent chat from the sidebar onto a Project row to add it. You can also open the chat's sidebar menu and choose **Add to Project**. If the action is available for a local chat, Cursor converts it to Remote Control before adding it." To take a chat back out, choose **Remove from Project** from its menu in the Agents list.

The docs don't say when **Add to Project** is available for a local chat. If it doesn't appear for this chat, they describe no other way to move it.

**3. The web (cursor.com/agents)**

The docs give no web UI steps for creating a Project or moving a chat into one. The web is only mentioned as where you can view a Project, at a `cursor.com/agents/bc-…` URL.

The other documented route is the API: `POST /v1/projects` with `name: "Semiconductor"` and `repos: [{ "url": "https://github.com/wolf359-ai/semiconductor" }]`. It needs a user API key, and there's no endpoint for adding an existing chat to a Project. See [Create A Project](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#create-a-project).
